end.parentNote: Harsh practised reading x first and y second, then using coordinate signs to identify the quadrant. They correctly identified Quadrant IV for (+,−), Quadrant II for (−,+), and the y-axis when x = 0. They initially mixed up (3, 2) and (2, 3), but corrected this after using the column-and-row example and later explained that the points are different. At home, ask them to plot two swapped pairs such as (2, 3) and (3, 2) and describe how their positions differ.
